The Most Serene Hohenlohe Patrimonial Court hereby makes known that between the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld, as general attorney of His Serene Highness the reigning Prince of Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen on the one part, and Blazy Kukulski on the other part, the following contract of sale and purchase has been concluded and published concerning one Hufe of land, Magdeburg measure, situated by the estate of Osiny.

Actum Trąbczyn, the eighteenth of July, one thou

sand eight hundred and

six.

Before the undersigned local Patrimonial Court there appeared in person

firstly

1. the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld, as general attorney of His Serene Highness the reigning Prince of Hohenlohe-Ingefingen, sole hereditary lord and lord of the court, legitimated by the [uncertain: attached] power of attorney, of the one part, and

2. the farmer Blazy Kukulski from the princely estate of Osniy, of the other part. The appearing parties are precisely known to the undersigned justiciary, and their capacity to perform judicial acts is subject to no doubt. They declare, freely and after due deliberation, the following hereditary lease contract concluded between them, irrevocable

and in nothing to be altered, which they hereby forthwith publish to the judicial protocol.

§. I. His Most Serene Highness namely grants to Blazy Kukulski

1 Hufe, in words one Hufe Magdeburg measure, the Hufe reckoned at thirty Morgen and each Morgen at one hundred and eighty square rods, at Kotikale Czazy w Kierzäwn arable land situated near Osiny, in hereditary lease for perpetual time.

§. II. Huba Maydebuska, and this one Hufe Magdeburg measure has already been assigned to Blazy Kukulski and delivered into actual possession

with which he is entirely content.

§. III. Blazy Kukulski pays for this one Hufe Magdeburg measure as purchase money 100 Rthl, in words one hundred Reichsthaler, and since he has already discharged this purchase money in full, he is hereby receipted for it.

§. IV. Besides this, Blazy Kukulski hereby binds himself, for himself and his successors in possession, to pay to the ground lordship an annual hereditary rent of 30 Rthl, in words thirty Reichsthaler, in ready current Courant, from this one Hufe Magdeburg measure, and this hereditary rent shall now and

in future be discharged in half-yearly instalments, namely the one at Midsummer and the other at Christmas, each time post numerando, and the first half-yearly hereditary rent shall not be paid until Christmas 1806.

§. V. The settlement and rendering of the royal and other public dues falling upon this one Hufe, without any distinction, as also the chimney money, forage delivery and carting service, the hereditary lessee takes upon himself now and for perpetual time, without any deduction from the hereditary rent, or demanding any reimbursement for it from the ground lordship.

In return the hereditary lessee is now and for perpetual time entirely free of all and every manorial labour service, as also of hereditary subjection.

§. VI. The hereditary lessee must establish and build his settlement entirely at his own cost, and receives for this neither now nor in future any building timber or other building assistance, and just as little any remission of the annual hereditary rent; however, all the timber standing on this Hufe remains without exception his property, and he may dispose of it without restriction.

§. VII. Outside his own holding the hereditary lessee has no right

to firewood or pasturage in the manorial woods and fields.

§. VIII. The hereditary lessee must always take his drink from the manorial brewery and distillery or from the inn.

If foreign drink is brought in by him or his people, the hereditary lessee incurs each time a penalty of five Reichsthaler for every barrel of beer and one Reichsthaler for every garniec of brandy, which penalty is to be paid to the ground lordship as compensation.

§. IX. The hereditary lessee remains always subject to the jurisdiction of the ground lordship, as also to the milling obligation on the manorial estates.

§. X. The hereditary lessee is entitled to dispose of this holding and to alienate it otherwise at his pleasure.

The ground lordship, however, hereby reserves to itself once and for all the right of pre-emption, and if it will not exercise the same, then the tenth Groschen of the purchase or exchange sum must be paid by each respective seller to the ground lordship as a transfer fee (Laudemium).

On inheritances to children and other relatives no transfer fee is paid.

§. XI.

The hereditary lessee renounces entirely, for himself and his successors in possession, all and every remission in cases of misfortune, whether these arise through fire from heaven, arson by evil people, hailstorm, crop failure, cattle plague, war and pestilence, or in whatever manner it may be, and in such cases there shall be neither any allowance nor

remission of the hereditary rent.

§. XII. His Most Serene Highness consents that the hereditary lessee may have the title of possession of this one Hufe thus acquired entered in his name in the land and mortgage book on the ground of this contract.

§. XIII. The purchaser undertakes to settle the whole of the costs attending this contract.

§. XIV. So long as the hereditary lessee and his successors in possession fulfil all the obligations contained in this contract, His Most Serene Highness promises to maintain them in their rights and to defend them against any man's real claim. But should the hereditary lessee or his successors in possession remain in arrears with the annual hereditary rent for longer than two years,

or lay this holding waste and thereby diminish the revenues of the ground lordship, then the ground lordship shall be entitled to let out this holding otherwise, and the hereditary lessee thereupon forfeits the whole right, and the purchase moneys paid in remain the property of the ground lordship.

Both parties promise to keep this contract firmly and inviolably; having been judicially instructed as to the consequences, they renounce all evasions available against it, particularly the objection of an injury suffered above and below the half, of cunning persuasion, fear, coercion, of matters otherwise agreed than written down or not rightly understood; they applied to have this contract confirmed and an official copy made out, and after it had been

read out in the German and Polish languages, they have in token of approval subscribed and signed below in their own hands.

General power of attorney. I, the undersigned, hereby make known and confess that I expressly empower the Royal Councillor of War and Forests Peter Friedrich August von Triebenfeld, Your Right Honourable, of Schweinern etc., to attend, both judicially and extrajudicially, to all and every matter in my name touching my estates of Zagorowo, Witów and Trąbczyn situated in South Prussia in the Kalisz Department, whether they concern a dismemberment or purchase and sale, leasing or pledging, or by whatever other name they may go and with which they may have connection and bearing; to petition for and respectively to notify all approvals or instructions necessary in that regard, as also all other requisites appearing to him necessary, both with the most laudable Chamber and with the most laudable

Government at Kalisz and with all other authorities, and to attend to all other requisite business for me, to come to terms with the tenants and conclude settlements, to pay moneys, to receive the like and to give receipts for them, to issue to my officials and servants there the orders serviceable to his purpose, to investigate their conduct and performance of service, and if in his judgement he should find such [conduct] fitting and prejudicial to me, to suspend them if need be, and generally to act without restriction and freely with all authorities and in all matters as he shall find good and most conducive to my interest. Whatever my said authorised representative shall do by virtue of this commission received, I hereby promise to approve and to hold to it as inviolably as though I had done it myself. At the same time I also bind myself to indemnify my authorised representative in every respect on account of this commission, and to make good to him all costs and outlays, on the pledge of my present and future estate so far as shall be required for this purpose. [illegible]

In witness whereof I have subscribed this general power of attorney in my own hand and confirmed it by the impression of my arms. Done at the Guhrwitz Justice Office near Breslau, the 19th February 1805.

(L. S.) read by myself and approved, Fridrich Ludwig, Prince of Hohenlohe. That His Serene Highness the reigning Prince and Lord, very well known in person to the undersigned Justice Office and fully capable of disposing, General of Infantry, Chief of a Regiment, Governor of the city and fortress of Breslau and Knight of the Great Black and of the Red Eagle Orders, Fridrich Ludwig, Prince of Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, drew up the foregoing general power of attorney directed to the Royal Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld this day before us and with our participation, acknowledged himself throughout to the literal content of the same, and thereupon, after His Highness had once more read it through beforehand and approved it, subscribed and sealed it in our presence in his own hand. The same is hereby testande Protocolli de hodierno in fidem publicam att[ested]

summary_en: A hereditary-lease contract granting the farmer Blazy Kukulski one Hufe of arable land, Magdeburg measure, near the estate of Osiny, made before the Hohenlohe patrimonial court by Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld for the Prince of Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen: 100 Rthl purchase money already paid, 30 Rthl yearly rent from Christmas 1806, public dues, milling and drink obligations on the lessee, freedom from labour service, and the lordship's pre-emption and tenth-Groschen transfer fee. Filed with it is Triebenfeld's 1805 general power of attorney for Zagorowo, Witów and Trąbczyn.
summary_de: Erbpachtvertrag in vierzehn Paragraphen über eine Hufe Magdeburgischen Maßes (30 Morgen) bei Osiny, geschlossen vor dem Hohenlohischen Patrimonialgericht zwischen dem Kriegs- und Forstrat von Triebenfeld als Generalbevollmächtigtem des Fürsten Friedrich Ludwig zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen und dem Bauern Blazy Kukulski: Kaufgeld 100 Rthl, bereits gezahlt, dazu jährlich 30 Rthl Erbzins in halbjährlichen Raten ab Weihnachten 1806, Freiheit von Frondiensten, aber Bier- und Mühlenzwang, Laudemium des zehnten Groschen und Vorkaufsrecht der Gutsherrschaft. Beigefügt sind die Vollmacht von 1805 und eine beglaubigte Abschrift.
